fullAnalysis: Puzzle #675 points to "Types of signs" because each clue naturally becomes a sign phrase that people already recognize.
Street sign, warning sign, and peace sign make the rule obvious quickly. Vital signs and equal sign widen the board into health and math, but the shared connector still holds cleanly.

wordHints.warning: Warning sign is a direct and very common phrase.
wordHints.street: Street sign is one of the easiest anchors in the set.
wordHints.vital: Vital signs belongs to the same family in a medical context.
wordHints.peace: Peace sign is a fixed cultural symbol phrase.
wordHints.equal: Equal sign completes the set in a mathematical context.

lessons.title: Test the most ordinary phrase ending first
lessons.body: Easy boards often rely on very common phrase endings. When clues feel everyday and familiar, reach for the simplest connector rather than hunting for something clever.

lessons.title: Different domains can share one clean connector
lessons.body: Street, warning, peace, vital, and equal come from traffic, safety, culture, medicine, and maths — but sign works for all of them. A puzzle stays clean even if the clues span different areas of life.

lessons.title: Vital signs is plural — and that's fine
lessons.body: Vital signs uses the plural form while the other clues pair with a singular sign. Pinpoint allows this variation; the connector still counts if the compound phrase is standard.

faqs.question: Why does vital belong with sign?
faqs.answer: Vital signs is a standard phrase in medicine, which keeps sign as the shared connector.

faqs.question: Was this an easier puzzle than recent boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, the common phrase set is much more direct than the trickier phrase-family boards around it.
